defect/JGS23-ONEPOPULATION-CDF-EXPONENT-.source_reading: The one-population corollary gives support through N^(1/beta) but prints F(q) = (q/N)^(beta/(P-1)).

defect/JGS23-ONE-DIMENSIONAL-UNIQUENESS-.source_reading: The labelled one-dimensional example asserts that its displayed power-law distribution is the unique symmetric equilibrium.

defect/JGS23-ZERO-GENRE-NORMALIZATION-01.source_reading: Genre is defined as p / ||p|| for every p in topological support, without excluding zero.

defect/JGS23-NECESSARYSUFF-TIE-NULLNESS-.source_reading: The necessary-and-sufficient characterization replaces expected winner mass by marginal maximum CDFs without a score-tie nullness condition.
defect/JGS23-NECESSARYSUFF-TIE-NULLNESS-.memo_heading: Two-user characterization, phase results, and profit

defect/JGS23-PHASE-TRANSITION-REGULARITY.reason: The score-law, CDF, and conditional radial regularity used by Theorem 2 are stated in the paper, so restating them does not narrow its economic domain.

defect/JGS23-INFINITE-GENRE-LIMIT-MODEL-.source_reading: The infinite-producer limiting discussion uses inconsistent indices and the named theorem assumes an angle arccos(...) < 0 and weights alpha_1 = alpha_2 = 2 while requiring weights to sum to one.

defect/JGS23-INDUCED-COST-GENERAL-DIMENS.source_reading: The induced-cost display is stated for two linearly independent users in arbitrary dimension as though the score pair determines the Euclidean production cost.
defect/JGS23-INDUCED-COST-GENERAL-DIMENS.memo_heading: Two-user characterization, phase results, and profit

defect/JGS23-NONZERO-SPAN-IMPLICATION-01.source_reading: Lemma nonzero says that a singleton genre lies in the span of the users, parenthetically treating that as implying strictly positive score against every user.

defect/JGS23-SINGLE-GENRE-PROFIT-REGULAR.source_reading: Proposition zeroutilitysinglegenre states that every single-genre equilibrium has zero expected profit.
defect/JGS23-SINGLE-GENRE-PROFIT-REGULAR.memo_heading: Two-user characterization, phase results, and profit

defect/JGS23-SUPPORT-RESTRICTION-NORMALI.reason: Positive rescaling of each user preserves score rankings and ties, so unit-score normalization preserves Proposition 4's mathematical content.

defect/JGS23-UTILITY-PROFIT-BRIDGE-01.source_reading: Proposition utility concludes that every symmetric equilibrium has strictly positive profit from the displayed geometric condition.
defect/JGS23-UTILITY-PROFIT-BRIDGE-01.memo_heading: Two-user characterization, phase results, and profit

defect/JGS23-TWO-USER-CALCULUS-DOMAIN-01.source_reading: The FOC, secondderiv, and regionscolor lemmas state derivative, sign, and support-curve conclusions for arbitrary-dimensional nonnegative users using C1--C3 without stating derivative-base, graph, density, or SOC hypotheses.
defect/JGS23-TWO-USER-CALCULUS-DOMAIN-01.memo_heading: Two-user characterization, phase results, and profit

defect/JGS23-SUPINF-ATTAINMENT-01.source_reading: Lemma supinf claims the ratio sup-inf identity for every subset of the strictly positive orthant, including a proof sketch that treats a product argmax as available or approximable without compactness.

defect/JGS23-OPTIMIZATION-MINIMAX-DOMAIN.source_reading: The informal optimization-program lemma equates a single-genre equilibrium condition with an inf-sup equals sup-inf ratio expression; its appendix restatement parameterizes the same display by Ball_m.

defect/JGS23-OPT-SINGLE-DIRECTION-IDENTI.source_reading: Lemma optsingledirection identifies the existence of a symmetric equilibrium with genre {p*} with a ratio bound, then argues through the CDF that the equilibrium must be the canonical ray law.

defect/JGS23-CONDITIONGEN-INFIMUM-ATTAIN.source_reading: Lemma conditiongen states an infimum-over-Ball_m ratio condition for single-genre equilibrium existence without separately stating a minimizer or the regularity used by its fixed-direction and CDF arguments.

defect/JGS23-BETASTAR-COROLLARY-ENDPOINT.source_reading: The beta-one, beta-p, and beta corollaries package their conclusions through beta-star even though the source defines beta-star only as a supremum and does not separately establish endpoint attainment or the regularity used by the single-genre route.

convention/JGS23-FINITE-DIMENSIONAL-NORM.reason: A finite-dimensional norm has continuous, measurable, compact bounded sublevels and convex balls; recording these norm properties does not add an economic hypothesis.
